topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text: Rain was still drumming against the window when I got the call. My contact's voice was small, almost lost in the static. Friend of his, see, been spinning yarns about what he did for a living. Turned out, the job was as real as a three-dollar bill. Got me thinking, the lengths folks'll go to keep up appearances. Money talks and all, but when it whispers, the lies get loud. Told him I'd poke around, maybe shine a light on why the story didn’t add up. But I already knew the root of it – the need to fit in, to be someone. Ain’t that the story of the city? Every face a mask, every smile a lie. I promised to call back with something more than shadows.
